title: Clean SVG Code Optimization & Press-Ready PDF/X
subtitle: viewBox Precision, Font Embedding Rules, PDF/X-4 & Commercial Bleed Setup

learningObjectives: Audit and optimize SVG export presets to output clean, lightweight, semantic vector code with responsive viewBox coordinates.
Calibrate SVG decimal precision, transform flattening, and font outline conversion to eliminate bloated base64 raster blobs.
Distinguish between PDF/X-1a (flattened legacy press) and PDF/X-4 (modern live transparency press) standards.
Configure commercial document bleed (3mm / 0.125 in) and output printer crop marks, registration targets, and color bars.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: The culmination of professional vector mastery is the delivery of flawless production assets tailored to their ultimate destinations: either clean, semantic SVG code for digital developers or bulletproof, color-calibrated PDF/X documents for commercial offset printers. A poorly configured SVG export can inadvertently embed megabytes of base64 bitmap data or include non-responsive hardcoded pixel dimensions that break web layouts. Similarly, sending a standard digital PDF to a commercial print house without bleed or trim marks causes white paper edges and misregistration on high-speed guillotine cutters. Mastering SVG code optimization and PDF/X commercial standards completes the full-spectrum Designer toolchain.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure Document Bleed for Commercial Print
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: In Designer Persona, press Ctrl+Alt+P (Cmd+Option+P) to open Document Setup. Switch to the 'Bleed' tab. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right bleed according to your print vendor's mechanical guidelines (commonly 3 mm in metric regions or 0.125 inches in imperial regions). Click OK. Notice the outer cyan bleed margin guide appearing around your canvas.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Open the Master Export Dialog
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S (Windows) or Cmd+Option+Shift+S (macOS) to open the comprehensive Export modal dialog.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Calibrate Clean SVG Web Code
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Select the SVG icon. From the Preset dropdown, choose 'SVG (for web)'. Click the 'More' button to inspect advanced markup rules: Ensure 'Use viewBox' is checked, set 'Decimal Places' to 2, check 'Flatten transforms', set 'Text' to 'Convert to curves', and set 'Rasterize' to 'Nothing'. Click Close.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Inspect Raw SVG Markup in a Text Editor
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Export the SVG file. Open it inside a text editor (e.g. VS Code). Verify that the file begins with a clean `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">` tag, uses pure `<path d="...">` coordinates without `matrix(...)` clutter, and contains zero `<image src="data:image/png;base64...">` bloated raster blobs!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Generate Press-Ready PDF/X-4 with Printer Marks
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Re-open File > Export. Select PDF. Set Preset to 'PDF/X-4:2010'. Click 'More'. Under 'Raster DPI', confirm 300 DPI. Mandatory: Under 'Bleed and Marks', you MUST check 'Include bleed' (otherwise Affinity clips output to page trim regardless of Document Setup bleed!). Also check 'Include printer marks', 'Crop marks', and 'Registration marks'. Color space: CMYK. Click Export.

visualExamples.title: PDF/X Standards Comparison Matrix
visualExamples.description: Technical differences between ISO PDF/X commercial print standards.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| Standard | Year | Color Spaces Allowed | Transparency Handling | Recommended Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDF/X-1a | 2001 | CMYK and Spot Colors only (RGB forbidden) | Flattened (All drop shadows and blend modes baked to bitmaps) | Traditional legacy offset presses, strict newspaper publishing |
| PDF/X-3 | 2002 | CMYK, Spot, and Color-Managed RGB | Flattened (Requires transparency flattening) | European commercial color-managed workflows |
| PDF/X-4 | 2010 | CMYK, Spot, RGB, and 16-bit Float | Live Transparency Preserved (RIP handles flattening at press time) | Modern commercial presses, packaging, high-end magazines, fine art |

visualExamples.title: Clean SVG vs Bloated SVG Code Snippet
visualExamples.description: Comparison of optimized markup versus un-optimized exporter output.
visualExamples.visualContent:
<!-- OPTIMIZED CLEAN SVG (viewBox, 2 decimals, flattened) -->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
  <path d="M12 2L2 22h20L12 2zm0 3.8L18.5 20H5.5L12 5.8z" fill="#4f46e5"/>
</svg>

<!-- BLOATED DIRTY SVG (Fixed px, 6 decimals, base64 image blob) -->
<svg width="24px" height="24px" viewBox="0 0 24.000000 24.000000">
  <image width="24" height="24" href="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAA..."/>
</svg>

commonPitfalls.mistake: Unchecking 'Use viewBox' when exporting SVG for responsive web development.
commonPitfalls.consequence: The SVG embeds hardcoded width='500px' height='500px' attributes, preventing CSS from scaling the icon responsively.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always check 'Use viewBox' in the SVG export settings so developers can scale the vector cleanly via CSS.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Using unsupported layer effects (like Gaussian Blur) and setting Rasterize to 'Everything'.
commonPitfalls.consequence: The SVG is no longer vector; it becomes a massive base64-encoded bitmap wrapped in an SVG tag.
commonPitfalls.solution: In SVG export settings, set 'Rasterize: Nothing' or use pure vector gradients instead of heavy raster blurs for web assets.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Sending a PDF to a commercial printer without checking 'Include bleed'.
commonPitfalls.consequence: The printer's guillotine blade may cut 0.5mm off-center, leaving an unsightly white hairline border along the trimmed paper edge.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always set 3mm bleed in Document Setup, extend background artwork to the bleed guide, and check 'Include bleed' when exporting PDF.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is the 'Use viewBox' attribute essential when exporting SVG graphics for modern web and mobile applications?
options: It forces the SVG to open only in Adobe Acrobat.
It defines the relative aspect ratio and coordinate system, allowing the SVG to scale smoothly to any dimension via CSS without hardcoded pixel limits.
It converts the SVG into a 3D stereoscopic format.
It reduces the color palette to 16 colors.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The viewBox attribute defines the vector coordinate boundaries (e.g. `viewBox='0 0 24 24'`), allowing CSS and HTML to resize the icon responsively to any width or height.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary difference between the PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4 commercial printing standards?
options: PDF/X-1a requires all transparency to be flattened and permits only CMYK/Spot colors; PDF/X-4 supports modern live transparency and color-managed workflows.
PDF/X-1a is for web only; PDF/X-4 is for laser printers only.
PDF/X-4 can only be opened on macOS.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: PDF/X-1a is an older standard that flattens all transparencies into static CMYK pixels at export; PDF/X-4 is the modern standard that preserves live vector transparency and handles RIP flattening at the press.

knowledgeCheck.question: How much bleed margin is standard for international commercial offset printing?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The international commercial standard for document bleed is 3 mm (or 0.125 inches in imperial regions), which accommodates minor physical paper shifting during mechanical guillotine trimming.

keyTakeaways: Optimized SVGs require responsive viewBox attributes, 2 decimal precision, and flattened transforms.
Avoid base64 SVG bloating by setting 'Rasterize: Nothing' and relying on native vector paths.
PDF/X-4 is the definitive modern standard for commercial press printing with live transparency.
Always configure 3mm bleed and include printer crop marks to prevent white trim defects.

slides.title: The Final Frontier: Production Output
slides.subtitle: Engineering Assets for Web, Mobile & Commercial Press
bullets: A brilliant vector illustration is only as good as its final exported delivery.
Digital developers demand clean, lightweight, semantic SVG code.
Commercial printers demand certified, color-accurate PDF/X documents with bleed.
Affinity Designer provides industry-leading export engines for both worlds.
slides.proTip: Mastering production settings eliminates 99% of developer friction and printer rejection.

slides.title: Anatomy of an Optimized SVG
slides.subtitle: Clean Semantic Code vs Bloated Markup
bullets: A clean SVG contains pure mathematical paths: `<path d='M12 2L2 22...' fill='#4f46e5'/>`.
A bloated SVG contains huge base64 images: `<image href='data:image/png;base64...'/>`.
Bloated SVGs occur when unsupported layer effects force the exporter to rasterize.
Clean SVGs load in milliseconds, scale infinitely, and can be styled with CSS.
slides.callout: In SVG export settings, always set 'Rasterize: Nothing' to prevent bitmap embedding!

slides.title: Essential SVG Settings: The 'More' Dialog
slides.subtitle: Precision Markup Calibration
bullets: Preset: Choose 'SVG (for web)' as your baseline.
Use viewBox: Checked (Removes hardcoded width/height for fluid CSS responsiveness).
Decimal Places: Set to 2 (Saves up to 40% file size without visible degradation).
Flatten Transforms: Checked (Bakes matrices into path coordinates for cleaner DOM).
Text: 'Convert to curves' guarantees exact font rendering on all client machines.
slides.proTip: Inspect your exported SVG in VS Code or Chrome DevTools to verify its markup cleanliness.

slides.title: Commercial Print: Why We Need Bleed
slides.subtitle: Preventing Unsightly White Paper Edges
bullets: Commercial presses print multiple pages onto giant sheets of paper, then cut them with high-speed guillotines.
Guillotine blades can drift by 0.5mm to 1mm during physical trimming.
Bleed is the extra 3mm margin of artwork extending OUTSIDE the final cut line.
If the blade shifts slightly, it trims into the extra artwork instead of revealing raw white paper.
slides.callout: Never stop your background color at the document edge; always stretch it to the bleed line!

slides.title: Configuring Document Bleed (3mm Standard)
slides.subtitle: Document Setup Geometry
bullets: Open File > Document Setup... (Ctrl+Alt+P / Cmd+Option+P).
Switch to the 'Bleed' tab.
Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right to 3 mm (or 0.125 inches in imperial regions).
The canvas displays a cyan guide line indicating the outer bleed perimeter.
slides.proTip: Press Ctrl+; (Cmd+;) to ensure guides and bleed lines are visible on your canvas.

slides.title: Deciphering the PDF/X Standards
slides.subtitle: PDF/X-1a vs PDF/X-4
bullets: PDF/X-1a:2001: The traditional standard. Requires CMYK only; flattens all transparency into pixels.
PDF/X-4:2010: The modern standard. Supports live vector transparency, spot colors, and RGB color management.
Most high-end commercial printers today recommend PDF/X-4 for superior gradient and drop shadow reproduction.
Always check with your specific commercial print provider for their preferred ISO preset.
slides.proTip: When in doubt, PDF/X-4 delivers the highest visual fidelity with live transparency.

slides.title: Exporting Commercial PDF/X with Printer Marks
slides.subtitle: Crop Marks, Registration & Color Bars
bullets: Open File > Export... (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S / Cmd+Option+Shift+S) -> Select PDF.
Choose Preset: 'PDF/X-4:2010'. Click 'More'.
Check 'Include bleed' (Crucial: Omitting this will clip the PDF at the trim boundary!).
Check 'Crop marks' (Trim lines for the guillotine cutter).
Check 'Registration marks' (Alignment crosshairs for multi-color press plates).
slides.callout: Confirm Raster DPI is set to 300 DPI for any embedded textured raster passes!

slides.title: Hands-on Exercise: Final Production Package
slides.subtitle: Step-by-Step Production Practice

Set up a 3mm document bleed and stretch background art to the bleed guide.
